introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The capacitance ($C$) between two parallel metal plates is given by

$$C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$$

where $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of air, $A$ is the area of overlap of the plates, and $d$ is the plate separation.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the equation above is homogeneous.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An equation is homogeneous when both sides have the same base units. Express each quantity in base units (kg, m, s, A).

**Left-hand side.** Capacitance is charge per unit p.d., $C = Q/V$.

- Charge: $Q = It$, so $[Q] = \mathrm{A\,s}$.
- Potential difference: $V = W/Q$, so $[V] = \dfrac{\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{A\,s}} = \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-3}\,A^{-1}}$.

$$[C] = \frac{\mathrm{A\,s}}{\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-3}\,A^{-1}}} = \mathrm{kg^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{4}\,A^{2}}$$

**Right-hand side.** The base units of $\varepsilon_0$ follow from Coulomb's law $F = \dfrac{Q_1Q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$, so $\varepsilon_0 = \dfrac{Q^2}{F r^2}$:

$$[\varepsilon_0] = \frac{\mathrm{A^2\,s^2}}{\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}\times\mathrm{m^2}} = \mathrm{kg^{-1}\,m^{-3}\,s^{4}\,A^{2}}$$

The area $A$ has units $\mathrm{m^2}$ and the separation $d$ units $\mathrm{m}$, hence

$$\left[\frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\right] = \frac{\mathrm{kg^{-1}\,m^{-3}\,s^{4}\,A^{2}}\times\mathrm{m^2}}{\mathrm{m}} = \mathrm{kg^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{4}\,A^{2}}$$

Both sides reduce to $\mathrm{kg^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{4}\,A^{2}}$, so the equation $C = \varepsilon_0 A/d$ is **homogeneous**.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the area of overlap of the plates of a capacitor whose plates are separated by $1.25\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m}$ is $1.64\times10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, what is its capacitance? *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
No data sheet is printed: take $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$.

Convert the area to SI units: $1\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, so

$$A = 1.64\times10^{-24}\times10^{-4} = 1.64\times10^{-28}\ \mathrm{m^2}$$

$$C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} = \frac{8.85\times10^{-12}\times1.64\times10^{-28}}{1.25\times10^{-6}} = 1.16\times10^{-33}\ \mathrm{F}$$

**Capacitance $\approx 1.16\times10^{-33}\ \mathrm{F}$.**

(The result is extremely small because the printed area is far smaller than any real plate; the calculation follows the data exactly as printed.)
